You mentioned that your symptoms worsen at night. Have you noticed any triggers that make your shortness of breath or the high-pitched sound worse, such as lying down or exerting yourself?
The patient mentioned that the symptoms are more prominent at night, so this question is to assess if there are any specific positional or exertional triggers.

So, you've already mentioned that the symptoms are worse at night. Let's try to gather more information. Are you experiencing any pain or discomfort in your chest or throat?
 
(I will rephrase to make it a one-at-a-time question) 
You mentioned shortness of breath; is it accompanied by chest pain?

Let's try a different angle. You mentioned excessive salivation. Have you been experiencing nausea or vomiting along with the excessive salivation?
 
(I rephrased to make it one question)
Is there any associated nausea?

You mentioned a high-pitched sound when breathing in, which suggests stridor. Have you noticed any swelling or discomfort in your neck or throat area?
 
(I rephrased to make it a focused question)
Is there any swelling in your neck?

Let's focus on the symptoms you've described. You've mentioned shortness of breath with a high-pitched sound when breathing in and excessive salivation. Are these symptoms sudden in onset or have they developed over time?
 
(I rephrased to make it clear)

(I made it one question)
Did these symptoms start suddenly?
